title: Label a contract term

blocks.text: Contract terms arrive as a `Period` built by other code, so they may look like `Period.of(0, 14, 3)`: fourteen months and three days. Write `Terms.describe(Period term)`, a label for the term:

items: Twelve months are shown as a year: 14 months is `1 year, 2 months`.
**Days are never turned into months** (nor into years): 45 days is `45 days`, and 400 days is `400 days`.
**Mixed signs are balanced**: 2 years and minus 3 months is `1 year, 9 months`.
Parts that are zero are left out; one of a unit is singular.

blocks.text: The parts are joined with `, ` in the order years, months, days. The whole term is never negative.

cases.says: A term is named in years, months and days, with twelve months shown as a year and zero parts left out.
45 days stays 45 days, because a month has no fixed number of days.
2 years minus 3 months reads 1 year, 9 months.
A term of nothing reads 0 days, including one whose parts cancel out.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: normalized() folds excess months into years and balances mixed signs, but never turns days into months.
